related.name: Audio Dynamic Range & Data Rate Calculator

method: Headphone drive requirement from the published sensitivity spec and the load. Sensitivity is quoted either as dB SPL for 1 mW into the rated impedance or as dB SPL for 1 V rms across it, and the two are tied together by S(dB/V) = S(dB/mW) + 10 log10(1000 / R) for an impedance R, so both readings are shown. Power needed at a level L with H dB of headroom is 10^((L - S(dB/mW) + H) / 10) milliwatts. When the spec is per volt, the voltage is 10^((L - S(dB/V) + H) / 20) volts rms and the power follows from P = V^2 / R; either way the rms voltage is sqrt(P R), the current is V / R, and the peak swing is sqrt(2) times the rms value. Headroom multiplies voltage by 10^(H/20) and power by 10^(H/10), and every reported figure includes it. Accepted inputs: impedance 1 to 2000 ohms, sensitivity 70 to 140 dB SPL per mW or 90 to 145 dB SPL per V rms, listening level 60 to 130 dB SPL, headroom 0 to 24 dB; numbers outside those bounds, blank fields or text are refused with the reason. Results carry three significant figures and are scaled to W, mW, µW or nW, and to V or mV; current switches to µA below one milliamp. A voltage-based verdict calls a load phone-friendly at 0.5 V rms or less, dongle territory up to 2 V, desktop up to 7 V, and very hard to drive above that, and the table repeats the power and voltage for 90, 100, 110 and 120 dB plus the chosen level. Output impedance, damping factor, distortion, noise, amplifier matching and listening-duration guidance are not modelled. Everything is arithmetic in the browser: no storage, uploads or network.
